item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
NIŠ / PRISTINA - In the border regions between Kosovo and Serbia, illegal logging has evolved into a highly prevalent and complex issue, leaving visible damage that grows more apparent over time.

From Kuršumlijska Banja on one side of the border to the villages of Podujeva on the other, local residents share the same unsettling reality. Radivoje Đorđević, who spent fifteen years doing this for a living, notes that unlike legal, regulated forestry, illegal logging is completely indiscriminate. Just across the border line in Hertica, hundreds of hectares of public forests are now on the verge of total destruction, with unpaved roads providing easy access for transporting timber.

Data from state forest enterprises reveals a staggering volume of illegally cut timber since 1999, resulting in billions of RSD in losses and immense environmental degradation. Despite these severe consequences, the phenomenon continues due to complex socio-economic factors, lenient court fines, and significant institutional challenges in cross-border coordination.

What is the exact scale of the timber volume lost over the years? How are local police and forestry agencies tackling this issue, and why have some key ministries failed to respond?

Key Findings:

  1. Scale and Financial Damage (1999–2025)
    Total Timber Volume: Between 1999 and 2025, a total of 1,160,600 m³ of timber was illegally cut down along the Kosovo–Serbia border in Serbia.
    Financial Loss: This activity represents a direct loss of 4,657,052,240 RSD (over 4.6 billion RSD), according to data from the "Srbijašume" State Forest enterprise.
    Visual Comparison: This volume of wood is enough to fill nearly 9 entire halls of the Palace of Youth and Sports in Pristina, 2.9 "Rajko Mitić" stadiums, or 3.3 JNA stadiums.
  2. Most Affected Locations and Forest Estates
    FE "Toplica" (Kuršumlija): Worst hit, accounting for 528,887 m³ of the illegally logged timber.
    FE "Šuma" (Leskovac): Ranks second with 340,198 m³.
    FE "Vranje" (Vranje): Ranks third with 256,134 m³.
    Other areas: FE "Šumarstvo" Raška recorded 27,686 m³, and FE "Rasina" Kruševac recorded 5,695 m³.
    Podujeva Region (Kosovo): In the Hertica–Turiqica region (compartment 128), around 510 hectares of public forest are on the verge of total destruction.
  3. Five-Year Trends (2021–2025)
    In the last five years alone, 117,088 m³ of timber volume was illegally cut along the border area.
    National Comparison: For context, during the same period across the entire Republic of Serbia, 41,349 m³ was logged in state forests and 115,929 m³ in private forests, highlighting the extreme intensity of logging specifically in the border zone.
  4. Methods and Drivers of Illegal Logging
    Indiscriminate Cutting: Unlike legal logging where only marked, sick, or crooked trees are cut, illegal logging clears everything in sight (primarily beech, oak, hornbeam, and Turkey oak for firewood).
    Infrastructure Factor: Poorly developed infrastructure and unpaved roads facilitate logging, as cutting happens right along roadsides for easy motor vehicle transport.
    Core Drivers: Multiple factors fuel the issue, including the socio-economic situation, high market demand for firewood, unresolved property-rights relations, and institutional gaps.
  5. Institutional Responses and Legal Obstacles
    Judicial Issues: Lenient fines and difficulties securing the burden of proof during court proceedings fail to deter illegal loggers.
    Police Records (2025): The Kosovo Police opened only 15 cases classified as “forest theft” in Podujeva, along with 4 additional cases reported by the Border Police.
    Institutional Silence: Neither Serbia’s Ministry of Internal Affairs nor Serbia's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, and Water Management provided responses to journalists.
    Kosovo Action Plan: The Kosovo Forest Agency (KFA) monitors timber transport but admits it faces difficulties combatting the issue in border areas without close coordination with the police, customs, and courts.
  6. Environmental Impact
    According to experts, clear-cutting and forest devastation alter species composition, change forest structure, and lead to nutrient depletion.
    Deforestation heavily degrades essential forest functions, including air purification, carbon dioxide binding, soil erosion protection, biodiversity preservation, and water regime regulation.

Methodology:

  • This research methodology combined quantitative and qualitative investigative journalism methods. The investigation began with desk research and data collection. This involved submitting official requests to state forest enterprises like Srbijašume and the Kosovo forest agency (KFA) to gather localized data on logged timber volume and estimated financial losses.
  • Once the documentary foundation was established, the methodology transitioned into field research and environmental documentation on the ground. We captured high-resolution photo evidence of illegal logging. This also included tracking the unpaved, informal roads.
  • The qualitative layer of the methodology relied on interviews to gather human testimonies. This included interviewing border village residents from areas like Kuršumlijska Banja and Podujeva to document eyewitness accounts of environmental changes and localized soil erosion. Furthermore, interviews were conducted with forestry professors and environmental scientists to detail long-term impacts. Before drafting the final report, rigorous fact-checking and data triangulation were applied.

Photo by Ganja Nikolić, Firewood

NIŠ / PRISTINA - In the border regions between Kosovo and Serbia, illegal logging has evolved into a highly prevalent and complex issue, leaving visible damage that grows more apparent over time.

From Kuršumlijska Banja on one side of the border to the villages of Podujeva on the other, local residents share the same unsettling reality. Radivoje Đorđević, who spent fifteen years doing this for a living, notes that unlike legal, regulated forestry, illegal logging is completely indiscriminate. Just across the border line in Hertica, hundreds of hectares of public forests are now on the verge of total destruction, with unpaved roads providing easy access for transporting timber.

Data from state forest enterprises reveals a staggering volume of illegally cut timber since 1999, resulting in billions of RSD in losses and immense environmental degradation. Despite these severe consequences, the phenomenon continues due to complex socio-economic factors, lenient court fines, and significant institutional challenges in cross-border coordination.

What is the exact scale of the timber volume lost over the years? How are local police and forestry agencies tackling this issue, and why have some key ministries failed to respond?

Key Findings:

  1. Scale and Financial Damage (1999–2025)
    Total Timber Volume: Between 1999 and 2025, a total of 1,160,600 m³ of timber was illegally cut down along the Kosovo–Serbia border in Serbia.
    Financial Loss: This activity represents a direct loss of 4,657,052,240 RSD (over 4.6 billion RSD), according to data from the "Srbijašume" State Forest enterprise.
    Visual Comparison: This volume of wood is enough to fill nearly 9 entire halls of the Palace of Youth and Sports in Pristina, 2.9 "Rajko Mitić" stadiums, or 3.3 JNA stadiums.
  2. Most Affected Locations and Forest Estates
    FE "Toplica" (Kuršumlija): Worst hit, accounting for 528,887 m³ of the illegally logged timber.
    FE "Šuma" (Leskovac): Ranks second with 340,198 m³.
    FE "Vranje" (Vranje): Ranks third with 256,134 m³.
    Other areas: FE "Šumarstvo" Raška recorded 27,686 m³, and FE "Rasina" Kruševac recorded 5,695 m³.
    Podujeva Region (Kosovo): In the Hertica–Turiqica region (compartment 128), around 510 hectares of public forest are on the verge of total destruction.
  3. Five-Year Trends (2021–2025)
    In the last five years alone, 117,088 m³ of timber volume was illegally cut along the border area.
    National Comparison: For context, during the same period across the entire Republic of Serbia, 41,349 m³ was logged in state forests and 115,929 m³ in private forests, highlighting the extreme intensity of logging specifically in the border zone.
  4. Methods and Drivers of Illegal Logging
    Indiscriminate Cutting: Unlike legal logging where only marked, sick, or crooked trees are cut, illegal logging clears everything in sight (primarily beech, oak, hornbeam, and Turkey oak for firewood).
    Infrastructure Factor: Poorly developed infrastructure and unpaved roads facilitate logging, as cutting happens right along roadsides for easy motor vehicle transport.
    Core Drivers: Multiple factors fuel the issue, including the socio-economic situation, high market demand for firewood, unresolved property-rights relations, and institutional gaps.
  5. Institutional Responses and Legal Obstacles
    Judicial Issues: Lenient fines and difficulties securing the burden of proof during court proceedings fail to deter illegal loggers.
    Police Records (2025): The Kosovo Police opened only 15 cases classified as “forest theft” in Podujeva, along with 4 additional cases reported by the Border Police.
    Institutional Silence: Neither Serbia’s Ministry of Internal Affairs nor Serbia's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, and Water Management provided responses to journalists.
    Kosovo Action Plan: The Kosovo Forest Agency (KFA) monitors timber transport but admits it faces difficulties combatting the issue in border areas without close coordination with the police, customs, and courts.
  6. Environmental Impact
    According to experts, clear-cutting and forest devastation alter species composition, change forest structure, and lead to nutrient depletion.
    Deforestation heavily degrades essential forest functions, including air purification, carbon dioxide binding, soil erosion protection, biodiversity preservation, and water regime regulation.

Methodology:

  • This research methodology combined quantitative and qualitative investigative journalism methods. The investigation began with desk research and data collection. This involved submitting official requests to state forest enterprises like Srbijašume and the Kosovo forest agency (KFA) to gather localized data on logged timber volume and estimated financial losses.
  • Once the documentary foundation was established, the methodology transitioned into field research and environmental documentation on the ground. We captured high-resolution photo evidence of illegal logging. This also included tracking the unpaved, informal roads.
  • The qualitative layer of the methodology relied on interviews to gather human testimonies. This included interviewing border village residents from areas like Kuršumlijska Banja and Podujeva to document eyewitness accounts of environmental changes and localized soil erosion. Furthermore, interviews were conducted with forestry professors and environmental scientists to detail long-term impacts. Before drafting the final report, rigorous fact-checking and data triangulation were applied.

Photo by Ganja Nikolić, Firewood

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
TULKARM - The Nitzanei Shalom industrial hub, built on Palestinian land in the mid-1980s, hosts Israeli factories. This investigation examines allegations that the hub is polluting the surrounding farmland, as well as its previously undocumented ties to European companies and markets.

Satellite imagery confirms what residents have been saying: a steady decline in biodiversity; major accidents, including fires, at industrial facilities; and a complete lack of wastewater management systems. In contrast, there are bales of gypsum and cement ready to be exported to Israel, some of which bear European logos. The companies that produce cement in Nitzanei Shalom are also involved in other businesses, including the export of weapons and warships to various parts of Europe.

The Nitzanei Shalom industrial zone is located on the western edge of Tulkarm, between the city and the separation wall. Established in the mid-1980s, it hosts Israeli factories operating on occupied Palestinian land. Over the past few decades, farmers, residents and workers have expressed concerns about the environmental and health impacts associated with the site.

Satellite imagery, planning documents, academic studies and fieldwork testimonies all point to the long-term transformation of the surrounding landscape. The images show how the industrial area has expanded into agricultural land, and researchers have documented soil, water and air contamination, including the presence of heavy metals and persistent industrial pollutants. Farmers describe a decline in agricultural productivity and an increase in restrictions on their access to land.

Satellite analysis also suggests an apparent lack of visible wastewater treatment infrastructure for industrial discharge, runoff and washing water. This fact is also proven by the testimony of farmer Fayez Taneeb, who had to pave a canal on his land to divert wastewater from the factories.

The investigation traces the commercial relationships between companies operating in the industrial zone and those in international markets. This includes establishing links to European business networks and supply chains.

Although the European Union considers Israeli settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territories (OPT) to be illegal under international law, commercial links between Nitzanei Shalom and European markets persist, highlighting the discrepancy between the EU's legal stance and the execution of its trade policies.

Aside from Alessandro and Filippo, the team included two Palestinian journalists, whose identities must remain secret for security reasons.

Key findings

  • Analysis of satellite imagery reveals the long-term expansion of the industrial zone into agricultural land, as well as a decline in the green spaces in the area. There appears to be an absence of visible wastewater treatment infrastructure.
  • Testimonies from residents, farmers and locals who have faced health and environmental harm from the industrial zone, such as land grabbing, crop damage, major fires and health issues.
  • Academic reports conducted upon the team's request from academics and researchers in Palestine and Italy to assess the previous studies conducted in this matter which explained that the environmental situation in Tulkarm may worsen if current pollution sources continue without effective mitigation, with the emphasis of the need for preventive measures, including continuous monitoring of water and soil, increased community awareness, safer agricultural practices, and the treatment of contaminated water before use.
  • Documentation of Israeli companies operating inside the industrial zone, including Israel Shipyards, Cement IS, Tambour, Orbond and other firms with limited public visibility in Europe.
  • Mapping of commercial, industrial and corporate links connecting companies in Nitzanei Shalom to European business networks and supply chains.
  • Several Israeli companies operating in Nitzanei Shalom maintain commercial and industrial relationships with European businesses, including companies based in Greece, Germany and Italy.
  • Gap between the European Union’s legal position on Israeli settlements and the continued existence of commercial relationships involving companies operating in occupied Palestinian territory.
  • Some companies operating in Nitzanei Shalom have links to Israel’s defence and military-industrial sector.

Methodology

The project was conducted using an interdisciplinary methodology that combined field reporting, visual work, academic review and document analysis with remote sensing. Fieldwork enabled direct observations to be made and contacts to be established with academic institutions and relevant governmental bodies in both Europe and Palestine. Reporting also involved engaging with civil society actors, whose testimonies helped to reconstruct local environmental and social conditions.

Satellite imagery analysis, supported by Planet.com and Placemarks, was used to evaluate the long-term spatial and environmental changes within and around the industrial zone. This was supplemented by an internal review of corporate structures and commercial links within Israel, as well as between Israeli companies and European markets.

In order to cross-reference sources and corporate data across jurisdictions, the research was conducted in multiple languages, including Hebrew, Italian, English, Arabic, Greek and Turkish. We also analysed official documents and databases used in recent major international investigations, and we had access to the experimental database of the Cross³ project.

Image © Alessandro Stefanelli: A road running alongside the Nitzanei Shalom industrial complex leading toward Palestinian agricultural lands. Tulkarem, West Bank, Palestine. Every morning at 6 a.m., farmers attempt to access their fields to work them, trying to avoid being seen by Israeli soldiers who restrict access and reportedly open fire when individuals are spotted.

Themes

  • Environment

Publication

  • Environmental Oppression in the West Bank: Is Europe Complicit?, Green European Journal, 23/06/2026
  • Israel’s Polluting West Bank Factories, New Lines Magazine, 23/06/2026

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
ROME - From human rights violations and forced labour to frequent illegal fishing, squid fishing in international waters is one of the least transparent food supply chains in existence. However, Europe and the United States are becoming the main buyers of squid linked to human rights violations and ecosystem destruction.

The Invisible Squid takes us on a journey into the world of the European seafood import and distribution industry. It reveals that seafood products linked to documented cases of human rights abuses, illegal fishing and forced labour are increasingly ending up on consumers' plates across Europe, particularly in Italy and Spain, as well as in the United States.

Our investigative team met with Spanish and Chinese producers, Chinese exporters, and intermediaries, wholesalers, restaurateurs and researchers from Europe and the US who analysed squid traded in the countries under study. We also conducted an in-depth data analysis to trace the journey of squid products from the Indian, Atlantic and Pacific oceans to restaurants in Italy's coastal cities, shops selling traditional sandwiches near Madrid's Plaza Mayor and supermarkets in California.

We found a supply chain characterised by a lack of transparency, weak regulation and an increasingly pervasive focus on achieving the 'best price'. This commercial environment simultaneously fuels demand for products whose supply chains conceal some of the most serious abuses, of which consumers remain largely unaware.

Key Findings

  • China is the world's leading exporter of squid and squid products. Despite numerous cases of unregulated fishing, regulatory violations and labour rights abuses being documented by journalists and non-governmental organisations in recent years, Chinese squid continues to be exported in growing quantities to the European Union, particularly Spain and Italy, and to the United States.
  • Chinese squid reaches consumers' tables in Europe with little transparency or consumer awareness. Ninety-eight percent of the squid consumed in Italy and Spain is frozen, yet it is often sold thawed by fishmongers alongside fresh seafood or served in restaurants without any indication of its origin.
  • China is expanding its share of Western markets by offering prices approximately 40% lower than those of European producers. This is partly due to the labour conditions on board fishing vessels and in processing facilities.
  • Several European companies have also partnered with Chinese producers to process squid in factories in China, despite documented evidence of forced labour programmes involving Uyghur workers and, in some cases, North Korean labourers.
  • The United States has curbed imports through tariffs on seafood products imported from China. By contrast, the European Union has not imposed comparable restrictions on seafood imports from China. However, the EU Forced Labour Regulation is due to come into force in 2027 and could have significant implications for this sector.

Photo by Francesco De Augustinis

Themes

  • Fishing industry
  • Environment

Publication

ONLINE

  • Il calamaro cinese «invisibile», dalle violazioni di diritti umani alle nostre tavole: così finisce nei ristoranti e nelle pescherie italiane, CorriereTV, 23/06/2026

  • Spain

Francesco De Augustinis

Francesco De Augustinis is an Italian freelance journalist and documentarist.

Guillermo Cid Rodríguez

Guillermo Cid is a Spanish senior reporter at El Confidencial.

Related projects

  • © Francesco de Augustinis

    The Invisible Factory Farms: The Rise of Aquaculture In "Green” Europe

    SUTHERLAND - The European Union pledged around 2.9 billion euro between 2001 and 2020 to support the development of aquaculture. Based on the Food and Agriculture Organisation's strong support for fish farming, European institutions plan to develop aquaculture in member states, in order to decrease imports of fish products, to produce food in a more sustainable way and to reduce overfishing and meat consumption.

    Meer lezen
  • © Arthur Debruyne

    Fish & Ships: Europe’s Fishing Deals In West Africa

    NOUAKCHOTT - In the imbalance of power in Europe’s fishing deals with West African countries, locals get the short end of the stick.

    Meer lezen
  • © Knack

    Illegal trade of pesticides and antibiotics in Europe

    BRUSSELS - There is a big illegal market for pesticides and antibiotics and these substances will still be spread, when they get banned. The industry has been able to continue the use of chlorpyrifos and expect the use to grow in the coming years, despite it has a huge and bad impact on animals and humans.

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
GUAYAQUIL – As European demand for tropical shrimp surges, Ecuador has become the continent's leading supplier. However, this booming industry exacts a heavy toll on vital mangrove ecosystems and the coastal communities that rely on them for their livelihoods.

Over the past two decades, Europe's appetite for shrimp has grown sharply. But local production meets barely one‑third of that demand, with the remainder coming from abroad. Once dominated by India and Vietnam, this market share is now led by Ecuador, which accounts for more than half of all imports. To keep up with rising demand, farms have pushed deeper into coastal areas already worn down by decades of mangrove deforestation. Between 1969 and 1999, as shrimp farming spread across the country, Ecuador lost as much as 43% of its mangroves.

Mangrove clearing is now banned in Ecuador, and the industry insists that habitat conversion has dropped to nearly zero despite soaring production. But while large‑scale clearance may be a thing of the past, residents of fenceline coastal communities – often among the country's poorest – and scientists say the destruction of mangroves is far from over. This investigation follows shellfish harvesters, crabbers, and fishers who depend on mangroves for their livelihoods as they describe smaller, harder‑to‑spot encroachments and other damage such as untreated wastewater discharged into estuaries.

Their testimonies are supported by satellite data, scientific studies and complaints showing that mangrove loss and ecological degradation have continued even inside legally protected areas. In numerous accounts, residents described environmental degradation so severe that it eroded their ability to feed their families. The story also examines Ecuador’s community mangrove custody agreements, a conservation model that gives local associations responsibility for protecting mangrove forests. While praised as innovative, the system often leaves poor communities to patrol, document and denounce damage with little support from the state.

Unlike the impacts of shrimp farming in Asia, which are well documented and have long attracted international scrutiny, Ecuador’s model has received comparatively little attention. And most European shoppers remain unaware that the frozen shrimp in their supermarket freezers may come from there. That information gap is partly structural: a 2024 report found that 63% of processed seafood products sold in the EU provide no country-of-origin information, while many of the remaining labels are incomplete or difficult to interpret.

Image by Vicente Gaibor: A shrimp farm discharging wastewater into a mangrove patch near Isla Costa Rica, a small island in the Jambelí Archipelago.

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
CONAKRY - Thanks to Chinese investments, the West African nation of Guinea is on track for annual economic growth of 10 percent. But Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah does not want the country to become too dependent on China and is also inviting Europe to invest.

Guinea is relatively unknown in Belgium, but this West African country is not only a major gold producer but also the world’s largest producer of bauxite. Day and night, giant machines scrape bauxite from the earth’s crust; trains and trucks continuously transport the ore to major river ports, from where it is shipped to China and Europe to be used in aluminum production.

According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Simandou will boost Guinea’s economic growth to 10 percent this year, one of the highest rates in the world. The government is therefore presenting “Simandou 2040” as the flagship project that will drive the country’s development. At the same time, the economic momentum is already exceeding the country’s capacity, with heavy traffic in and around the capital, Conakry.

Themes

  • Work
  • Youth

Publication

PRINT

  • 'Armoede hoeft niet onontkoombaar te zijn', MO*, Zomer 2026

Country

  • Guinea

Team members

John Vandaele

John Vandaele is a Belgian journalist with the monthly MO* magazine.

Layla Aerts

Layla Aerts is een Belgische freelance fotografe.

Related projects

  • © Derrick Boateng

    The Continent of the Future

    AFRICA - New generations always dream big. Daaf Borren travelled through some 16 countries in Africa, fascinated by their stories. From Mali and Congo to Ethiopia and Mauritania: this is an atypical travel book, in which you not only cover many kilometres, but also travel along to the future.

    Meer lezen
  • © divergente

    Game On

    LISBON – Each year, hundreds of African and South American minors come to Europe in search of a better life and professional success in the European football leagues, which they see as the new El Dorado. In doing so, they expose themselves to the cross-national, multimillion-dollar structures of power and quick profits.

    Meer lezen
  • © Eugenie D’Hooghe

    Violence by and against police in Brussels

    BRUSSELS - Protests against police are flaring up and are increasingly visible on the streets of Brussels. Among the demonstrators there are strikingly many young people. "We want change, and that only seems possible if we take matters into our own hands," shouts law student Amira (19), who is at the front of the demonstration following the death of Ibrahima Barrie on 13 January.

    Meer lezen

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
PRAGUE / ALYTUS / HELSINKI / ROME - The cross-border investigative project explores one of the least discussed consequences of Europe’s return to nuclear energy: what to do with radioactive waste that remains dangerous for tens of thousands of years.

Through reporting from the Czech Republic, Lithuania, Italy and Finland, the project examines how different European countries approach the long-term storage of spent nuclear fuel, how local communities respond to these plans, and what tensions arise between climate goals, energy security and environmental responsibility.

Main findings from the Czech reporting

  • The Czech government is accelerating plans for a deep geological repository for radioactive waste in connection with the expansion of nuclear energy and the prolonged operation of the Dukovany nuclear power plant. Experts warn that the expected volume of nuclear waste may exceed original assumptions.
  • Local communities in candidate regions strongly oppose the repository project. Residents and local officials say the state does not communicate transparently and is attempting to speed up the selection process without sufficient geological data and public consent.
  • Municipal representatives fear long-term impacts on water resources, regional development and quality of life. In the Hrádek locality near Dolní Cerekev, concerns focus especially on groundwater protection because the area lies near a major European watershed.
  • Critics argue that current Czech policy relies almost exclusively on permanent underground storage while giving insufficient attention to alternative approaches, including long-term monitored storage or future reuse of spent fuel.

Main findings from Finland

  • Finland is close to opening Onkalo, the world’s first permanent deep geological repository for spent nuclear fuel, after more than three decades of research, permitting and public consultations.
  • The repository is being built approximately 430 metres underground in stable granite bedrock and is designed to isolate radioactive waste for at least 100,000 years.
  • Finnish authorities and the company Posiva emphasize that long-term public trust was built through transparency, extensive communication and the strong role of municipalities in the approval process. Local communities effectively had veto power over the project.
  • Finland presents the repository as a practical solution linked to energy independence and long-term responsibility for nuclear waste generated domestically.

Main findings from Lithuania

  • On FM99 side we conducted a long and detailed interview with the head of the Visaginas nuclear power plant about the closure process. We also spoke with the head of the plant’s Sustainability Department about how dismantled parts of the closed power plant are turned into scrap metal or melted down into other metal products. Some of the sold parts are reused – this is how the recycling chain works, leaving less and less waste behind.

Photo by Kateřina Hefler, Březový potok one of possible places for nuclear depository

Themes

  • Energy
  • Environment

  • Úložiště na sto tisíc let. Finsko má způsob, jak skladovat vyhořelé jaderné palivo, a učí to i Čechy, Ekonews, 11/06/2026
  • Atominė elektrinė ruošiasi ardyti reaktorių, Visaginas – pradėti branduolinį turizmą, FM99, 14/06/2026

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
CHARLEROI / FARCIENNES - As Google rapidly expands its data centres in the Belgian region of Hainaut residents are watching farmland, wetlands and entire neighbourhoods disappear behind concrete walls and barbed wire.

While local politicians are praising the billions of pounds of investment and the promise of economic revival, residents, trade unions and environmental groups are questioning who will truly benefit. Research reveals growing concerns about energy consumption, land use, a lack of transparency, foreign subcontracting, and mounting pressure on Belgium’s electricity grid.

At the same time, Google is carefully cultivating a green and socially engaged image by investing in renewable energy, nature projects, and local cultural initiatives. However, critics see this as a sophisticated strategy to secure legitimacy for an industry with an increasingly heavy environmental footprint.

Through intimate portraits, field reporting and in-depth investigations, the series explores the contrast between the potential of artificial intelligence and the challenges faced by communities in the vicinity of hyperscale data centres.

Themes

  • Industry
  • Environment
  • Economy

Publication

PRINT & ONLINE

  • Enquêté sur l’expansion ambitieuse de Google en Wallonie, Médor, n°43, 04/06/2026

ONLINE

EVENT

Janine Meijer is a Belgian freelance journalist specializing in sustainability, social inequality and diversity.

Maïté Warland is a Belgian journalist since 2005.

Quentin Noirfalisse is a Belgian freelance investigative journalist and documentary filmmaker.

    European Data Centers' Rush for Land and Energy

    MILAN / BRUSSELS - As artificial intelligence expands across Europe, so does the demand for data centers. Traditionally hosted in cities like Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, and Dublin, these hubs are nearing full capacity. Milan, with its strategic location in the Mediterranean, is emerging as a key player.

    Meer lezen

    The Gold Trail

    ROSIA MONTANA - The Romanian village of Rosia Montana has been a site of historic gold and silver mining for over two millennia. Now, mining company Rosia Montana Gold Corporation plans a massive mining project, which is dividing the village into supporters and opponents.

    Meer lezen
  • © rr

    Gold Rush to Dam Balkan's Rivers

    SKOPJE - The Western Balkan countries, home to some of Europe's most pristine nature, are facing a rush to build new hydroelectric power stations.

Traditionally hosted in cities like Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, and Dublin, these hubs are nearing full capacity. Milan, with its strategic location in the Mediterranean, is emerging as a key player.

    The Gold Trail

    ROSIA MONTANA - The Romanian village of Rosia Montana has been a site of historic gold and silver mining for over two millennia. Now, mining company Rosia Montana Gold Corporation plans a massive mining project, which is dividing the village into supporters and opponents.

    Meer lezen
  • © rr

    Gold Rush to Dam Balkan's Rivers

    SKOPJE - The Western Balkan countries, home to some of Europe's most pristine nature, are facing a rush to build new hydroelectric power stations.

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
NARDÒ / STUTTGART – Natura 2000 constitutes the biggest network of protected natural areas in the European Union. But under the guise of public interest, these nature protection zones are increasingly being threatened by private industrial investments. It is the case of Nardò’s countryside, on the western coast of the heel of Italy's boot. Here, the Bosco d'Arneo, a Natura 2000 protected area, was threatened by the expansion project of the test drive circuit of the German company Porsche.

This investigation explores how the notion of public interest is stretched to fit private industrial interests in derogation of the European nature protection law, threatening the biodiversity of protected areas, specifically in Southern Italy.

In 2022, Porsche submitted an expansion plan for its test track in Southern Italy, the Nardò Technical Centre. The project involved clearing 200 hectares of forest and destroying Natura 2000 habitats in one of the last remaining forests in a region most affected by desertification in the Mediterranean.

To overcome this legal barrier, local authorities declared that the project had Imperative Reasons of Overriding Public Interest (IROPI), planning to construct a heliport and a sanitary station to "help strengthen the region's sanitary infrastructure and fight fire crisis". This seemed promising at first glance, as the EU Habitats Directive specifies "human health" and "public safety" as important motives of public interest.

However, after the European Commission requested a revision due to insufficient implementation of nature conservation measures, local authorities suspended the IROPI in 2024. Nevertheless, legal experts argue that the Commission is still not severe enough and tends to favour "imperative reasons of public interest" over nature conservation.

Although Porsche abandoned the investment plan a year ago, the closure agreement has been signed and suspended, but never cancelled. On paper, the company would have ten years to complete the runway. A citizens' committee, which opposed the expansion of the test track from the very beginning, continues to protect the forest.

Photo by Vittoria Torsello, Sheep belonging to a livestock farmer working inside the Nardò Technical Center testing track.

Themes

  • Environment

Publication

ONLINE

  • Come Porsche mette a rischio le foreste pugliesi, Lucy sui Mondi, 25/05/2026
  • In the “public interest”, but not in nature's, The European Correspondent, 25/05/2026
  • Naturschutz in Europa: Überwiegende private Interessen, RiffReporter, 20/06/2026

COUNTRIES

  • Italy
  • Germany

Team members

Vittoria Torsello is an Italian freelance journalist and co-founder of Marea Media.

Guillaume Amouret

Guillaume Amouret is a French journalist based in Hamburg.

Alessia Melchiorre

Alessia Melchiorre is a freelance journalist based in Italy.

Mentors

Elisângela Mendonça

Elisângela (Lili) Mendonça is a multimedia journalist based in London.

Related projects

  • Mikko Vähäniitty.

    Green To Grey: How Europe Is Squandering The Little Nature It Has Left

    LISBON / IZMIR / ROVANIEMI – In the first investigation of its kind, 41 journalists and scientists from 11 countries collaborated to measure nature loss across Europe using satellite imagery and artificial intelligence.

    Meer lezen
  • © Alex Kemman

    Green Veins of Europe: Ecocorridors and the European Green Deal

    EUROPE - From red deer traces and half wild horses, to ecoducts and tree plantations, till mountain ranges and free flowing rivers. They have something in common: these are the roads and routes that nature uses. 

    Meer lezen
  • © Velian Jagev

    Nature for Sale: Why Protection of Endemic Species Isn't Enforced

    SKOPJE - The Macedonian grayling is a unique butterfly species which resides exclusively on the outskirts of a small Macedonian town, with no other known locations worldwide. The specimen of this rare and endangered butterfly can be purchased at low prices across Europe — how did this become possible?

item.title: Meer lezen
item.description:
PRAGUE / KYIV – Across scarred landscapes where war has reshaped both land and lives, this cross-border series traces the invisible wounds left in soil and water and the fragile paths toward healing. From Ukraine’s frontlines to former Soviet military zones in Czechia, it follows how history lingers beneath the surface, and how places once defined by destruction can slowly return to life.

This cross-border series explores how military activity and war reshapes the landscape and how damaged land can be restored. By connecting current findings from Ukraine with Czech experience from former Soviet military zones such as Ralsko and Milovice, the project shows how traces of past use remain embedded in the environment, and what they reveal about the long, often fragile process of recovery.

Through field reporting, expert interviews and analysis of scientific data, the investigation maps the extent of soil contamination caused by heavy metals, explosives and oil residues. It compares ongoing research in Ukraine with decades of remediation efforts in Czechia, identifying both successful approaches and persistent challenges.

Main findings by Ekonews:

  • The Czech Republic has invested more than CZK 1.5 billion in the remediation of areas previously used by the Soviet army. Although the clean-up was expected to be completed by 2022, the process continues due to insufficient funding and the long-term complexity of contamination.
  • Czech researchers and companies are already active in Ukraine and have the expertise to contribute to environmental recovery. However, recent government decisions have limited financial support for their involvement, slowing down potential knowledge transfer.
  • Czech scientists are increasingly engaged in research on Ukraine’s environmental recovery. They stress that restoration will take decades, but that early mapping of damage, identifying both the sources and extent of contamination, is essential for planning effective and realistic clean-up strategies.

Summary from Rubryka:

The topic of soil restoration and decontamination has become particularly popular among scientists after the full-scale invasion, especially in the last two years. Various investigations are underway, some of them include attempts to regenerate soils with the help of vegetation, but so far everything is at the development stage, since such large-scale areas of contamination, as are currently present in Ukraine, require new approaches.

There is currently no state mechanism that would directly oblige to clean up territories from contamination caused by the war (except for mines).
Farmers use various methods for cleaning up land, and developing mechanisms will require further cooperation between farmers, scientists and representatives of state authorities.

Photo by CTK

Themes

  • Environment

Publication

ONLINE

  • Toxická půda po tancích a znečištěné podzemní vody. Některé bývalé vojenské areály ale už znovu žijí, Ekonews, 06/05/2026
  • Češi pomáhají s čištěním ukrajinské vody a půdy. Ze dne na den přišli o finance z rozpočtu, Ekonews, 26/05/2026

more to come

COUNTRIES

  • Czechia
  • Ukraine

Karolína Chlumecká is a journalist from the Czech Republic.

Irena Buřívalová

Irena Buřívalová is the editor of Ekonews (Czechia).

Viktoriia Hubareva

Viktoria Hubareva is an environmental journalist from Ukraine.

Maryna Smahina

Maryna Smahina is a Ukrainian author, media editor and trainer. 

Media

Ekonews

Ekonews is a website in the Czech Republic that deals with sustainability in the economy and in private life.

Rubryka

Rubryka is the first Ukrainian media outlet to focus on solutions journalism.

Related projects

  • © Philippe Pernot

    The Grainkeepers

    KYIV - Cereal is the new petroleum, farmland the new reservoirs of oil, and ships loaded with grain are the new pipelines. As the value of crops increases, every country in possession of this resource is in a position of power, and its transport to market is a politically-charged operation.

    Meer lezen
  • © Petru Zoltan

    The Cost of War for the Danube Delta

    CANAL BISTROE – Ukraine needs to defend itself using any means at its disposal. At the same time, the Danube Delta ecosystem must remain protected. Are these two demands mutually exclusive?

    Meer lezen
  • © Nikcenter.org

    The Black Sea in Peril: The Echoes of War Ripple Beyond Borders

    NOVA KAKHOVKA – In June 2023 the Russian military targeted Ukraine's Nova Kakhovka hydroelectric power plant, triggering an ecocide that strained the ecological resilience of the region. The polluted water added to the Black Sea's ongoing environmental degradation because of negligence and weak policies in the region.

    Meer lezen

item.title: حقيقة "غاز الكيمتريل": كيف تحولت آثار الطائرات إلى نظرية مؤامرة؟
item.description:
المصدر: AFP

منار أبو حسون


تنتشر على مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي منشورات لما يعرف بـ”نظرية الكيمتريل”، وازدادت وتيرة هذا النوع من الادعاءات بعد الحرب الإقليمية في المنطقة، حيث روجت عدة حسابات لمزاعم تفيد بأن الجو أصبح أصفى نتيجة تراجع حركة الملاحة الجوية، ورش “غاز الكيميتريل” في الجو من قبل الطائرات التجارية لأهداف خفية؛ مثل التحكم بالمناخ أو التأثير في صحة البشر. 

تعود هذه الادعاءات إلى أواخر تسعينيات القرن الماضي، ضمن قائمة الادعاءات المتعلقة بـ”نظريات المؤامرة” التي تقوم على  فرضية وجود مخطط سري تديره جهات نافذة؛ للسيطرة على الأحداث والظواهر العالمية. وغالباً ما ترفض هذه النظريات الروايات الرسمية أو الإجماع العلمي، وتقدم تفسيرات بديلة تفتقر إلى الأدلة الموثوقة. 

يكشف هذا التقرير أبرز الادعاءات عن نظرية “غاز الكيمتريل”، التي تداولتها حسابات عربية على منصة “إكس” بعد الحرب الإقليمية الأخيرة منذ 28 شباط/فبراير 2026، حتى تاريخ نشر هذا التقرير، ويفند هذه الادعاءات استناداً إلى المصادر العلمية الموثوقة. 

ماذا يزعم مروجو “نظرية الكيمتريل”؟

تتبعنا عدداً من السرديات والمنشورات بمحتويات مختلفة، تروّج للنظرية عبر محتويات متنوعة، شملت مقاطع فيديو وصوراً ومنشورات نصية. ومن أبرزها ادعاء نشره حساب “خديجة أحمد” التي تعرف نفسها على أنها صيدلانية تروّج عبر حسابها لادعاءات متعلقة بنظريات المؤامرة، ومنها الكيمتريل.

أبرز هذه الادعاءات، التي نشرها هذا الحساب وحصد آلاف التفاعلات، كان بتاريخ 24 نيسان/أبريل 2026، زعم أن “غاز الكيمتريل” يُعد أحد أسباب التغير المناخي.


لقطة شاشة من حساب “خديجة خالد” للادعاء


وجاء في نص الادعاء: “هذا ما تفعله أمريكا وإسرائيل، يسرقون الأمطار، ينتجون سحب اصطناعية، يقومون بتلقيح السحب وتغيير المناخ، يرشون مادة “الكيمتريل”(Chemtrail)، يستخدمون تقنية “هارب” (Haarp). ولكن إذا سألتهم، سيقولون لك إن التغير في المناخ طبيعي“.

في اليوم نفسه، ردّ حساب “زهراء رمضان” على منشور “خديجة أحمد” مؤيداً تلك المزاعم، مدعياً أن “الخطوط البيضاء التي تتركها الطائرات في السماء، ليست مجرد بخار ماء، بل هي مواد كيميائية (مثل الباريوم والألمنيوم) ترشها “نخب سرية” لتقليل عدد السكان أو التلاعب بالمناخ“. 

ويُعد هذا الادعاء من أكثر الروايات تداولاً ضمن نظرية “الكيمتريل”؛ إذ تُرفق منشورات من هذا النوع عادةً بصور أو مقاطع فيديو لآثار التكاثف التي تخلّفها الطائرات في السماء، مع الادعاء بأنها تمثل “غاز الكيمتريل”، أما تسميته فجاءت من كلمتي “Chemical trials” أي المسارات الكيميائية.


لقطة شاشة من ادعاء “زهراء  رمضان” و “موزه بنت عبيد”


وفي سياق مماثل، نشر أحد الحسابات المروجة لنظريات المؤامرة من الكويت، والذي يعيد عادةً نشر هذا النوع من المحتوى من حسابات أجنبية، ادعاءً في 9 حزيران/يونيو 2026، زعم فيه أن وثائق لوكالة المخابرات المركزية الأمريكية (CIA) كشفت عن خطط أميركية للسيطرة على العالم، عبر التلاعب بالطقس باستخدام ما يُعرف بـ”الكيمتريل”.


صورة من ادعاء qqqq8118 لمشاركة منشور حساب يدعى Stern Drew 


كما تناولت  العديد من الحسابات مزاعم أن الجو أصبح أنقى عقب إغلاق المجال الجوي، بسبب الحرب الإقليمية وتوقف رش “الكيمتريل“. ومن أبرز هذه الحسابات، حساب “دكتور ياسر خالد العمار“، الذي يعرّف نفسه بأنه جراح عظام كويتي يتابعه نحو 77 ألف متابع، ويتبنى الحساب منذ سنوات نظرية رش الكيمتريل لحجب أشعة الشمس والتلاعب بالمناخ، ونشر خلال الحرب عدة منشورات ادعى فيها أن السماء أصبحت أصفى مع توقف رش غاز “الكميتريل“.


صورة لمنشورات على ” اكس” تدعي توقف رش الكيمتريل بسبب الحرب



أبرز الحسابات التي رصدناها والتي تروج لادعاءات الكيمتريل:

د. ياسر خالد العمار
76.9 ألف متابع
جراح عظام كويتي
خديجة أحمد
20.9 ألف متابع
صيدلانية
موزه بنت عبيد
20.3 ألف متابع
أخصائية تقويم أسنان من الإمارات
STOP Age.2030
21 ألف متابع
حساب يهدف لنشر الوعي بأضرار اللقاحات وكشف مافيا الطب والعلم المزور وأهداف أجندة 2030.



عقد من التفنيد العلمي وما زالت ادعاءات المؤامرة حيّة!

رفض المجتمع العلمي هذه النظرية عام 2016، وصنفها ضمن “العلوم الزائفة”. حيث فندت دراسة علمية منشورة عام 2016 في مجلة Environmental Research Letters، بعنوان “قياس إجماع الخبراء ضد وجود برنامج سري واسع النطاق للرش الجوي” ادعاءات الكيمتيريل؛ إذ شملت استطلاع آراء خبراء في كيمياء الغلاف الجوي والترسبات الجوية، لتقييم الأدلة التي يستند إليها مروجو نظرية “الكيمتريل”.

وأظهرت النتائج أن 76 من أصل 77 خبيراً مشاركاً (بنسبة 98.7%) أكدوا أنهم لم يواجهوا أي دليل يدعم وجود برنامج سري واسع النطاق لرش مواد في الغلاف الجوي، كما أوضحوا أن الأدلة المتداولة لتأكيد هذه الادعاءات يمكن تفسيرها بظواهر معروفة علمياً، مثل آثار تكاثف الطائرات والهباء الجوي والعمليات الفيزيائية والكيميائية المرتبطة بالغلاف الجوي.

ولا تُعد هذه الادعاءات جديدة؛ إذ يمكن رصد تداول نظرية “الكيمتريل” باللغة العربية على منصة “إكس” منذ أكثر من عقد، بما في ذلك عبر بعض الحسابات الإعلامية منذ عام 2011.  واستمرت هذه المزاعم في الظهور بصورة متكررة خلال الأعوام 2018 و2023 و2024 و2025 رغم  تفنيدها سابقاً في تقارير تدقيق معلومات.


ما حقيقة الخطوط البيضاء التي تظهر كآثار للطائرات؟

أما الخطوط البيضاء التي تظهر خلف الطائرات عند تحليقها في السماء، والتي يستشهد بها مروجو هذه الادعاءات في صورهم ومقاطع الفيديو المتداولة، فيؤكد الخبراء أنها ليست سوى آثار تكاثف تُعرف علمياً باسم “مسارات التكاثف” (Contrails).

يجيب برنامج وكالة ناسا العلمي (NASA GLOBE) عن سؤال “لماذا قد نرى طائرة تصدر هذه الانبعاثات وطائرة لا تصدرها؟”، بأن السبب يعود لعاملي الرطوبة والارتفاع، اللذين تحلق فيهما الطائرات، وهو ما يحكم تشكل لمسارات التكاثف البيضاء التي نراها. 

ويوضح موقع البرنامج أن الطبيعة غير المتجانسة للغلاف الجوي، واختلاف نوع المحركات، عوامل مهمة كذلك؛ فإذا حلقت طائرة في طبقة هواء جافة، يتبخر عادمها المكون من بخار الماء فوراً دون أثر، في حين إذا حلقت في طبقة شديدة البرودة وعالية الرطوبة، يتجمد البخار فوراً مشكلاً خطوطاً جليدية بيضاء. 

ولم نجد ما يدعم علمياً وجود عناصر الباريوم والألمنيوم ضمن مواد عوادم الطائرات التجارية. ورغم أن قطاع الطيران يُسيّر ملايين الرحلات الجوية سنوياً، فإن نسبة ضئيلة منها فقط تُنتج آثاراً جوية تُؤثر بشكلٍ ملحوظ في المناخ، ولا تُحدث معظم الرحلات الجوية تأثيراً يُذكر. 


 لقطة من  فيديو لمنظمة الطيران الدولي المدني عبر يوتيوب لانبعاثات عوادم محركات الطائرات التجارية غير الكربونية


إلى جانب ذلك، تتميز المحركات النفاثة الحديثة بحرارة عوادم أبرد، وتطلق نسبة أعلى من بخار الماء، ما يجعلها علمياً أكثر عرضة لتكوين هذه الخطوط من المحركات القديمة، وفقاً لتقرير إدارة الطيران الفيدرالية الأمريكية (FAA). وقد رفضت الحكومة الأميركية مزاعم رشها لمركبات كيميائية في الهواء تؤثر في صحة السكان من قبل.


جزء من رد الحكومة الأميركية حول الادعاءات المرتبطة بمسارات التكاثف الناتجة عن الطائرات


ما حقيقة مقاطع الفيديو أو الصور المرفقة مع الادعاءات؟

المقطع الذي أرفقته “خديجة خالد” بزعم أنه لرش مواد سامة في الجو، تبين بالبحث العكسي أنه مقتطع من فيديو نشر على اليوتيوب عام 2016، يحمل عنوان “ТМС-65д”، وهو اسم آلة عسكرية روسية من طراز TMS-65؛ وهي آلة حرارية سوفيتية المنشأ صُنعت عام 1966 لصالح قوات الدفاع الإشعاعي والكيميائي والبيولوجي، تُستخدم لتطهير وتعقيم المعدات والمباني من المواد الكيميائية والبيولوجية، ومكافحة الآفات، بالإضافة إلى إنشاء ستائر دخانية لأغراض التمويه العسكري.

لقطة شاشة من موقع روسي يوضح استخدام المركبة 


أما المقال الذي ردت به “زهراء رمضان” على “خديجة”، بالبحث عنه تبين أنه مقال لراديو فرنسي، يؤكد أن غاز الكيمتريل يتبع نظرية المؤامرة، وكيف استخدمه سياسيون فرنسيون خلال تصريحاتهم.

وبخصوص  الوثيقة التي يزعم أنها لـ(CIA)، بمراجعة هذه الوثائق من وكالة المخابرات المركزية التي رُفعت عنها السرية، لا يوجد فيها ما يثبت وجود خطة أميركية للسيطرة على العالم من خلال التحكم بالطقس، أو رش مبيدات أو مواد في الجو، ولا توجد أي إشارة لاسم “الكيمتريل”، وفحوى الوثيقة حول طموحات التحكم بالطقس في ذلك الوقت عام 1965.


هل هناك أي برامج علمية موثقة لإطلاق مواد في الجو؟

أكدت مجموعة كيث في جامعة هارفارد عدم وجود أي أدلة موثوقة تدعم نظرية مؤامرة “الكيمتريل”، موضحةً أنه ربما قد يخلط بعض الناس بين مفهوم الكيمتريل والهندسة الجيولوجية المناخية.

في مقابلة تفصيلية أجراها موقع “Carbon Brief” مع عالمة المناخ، الدكتورة كاثرين هايهو، أكدت فيها بأن “الهندسة الجيولوجية ليست هي الكيمتريل”، مؤكدة أن “الكيمتريل” ما هو إلا “نظرية مؤامرة”.

أما الهندسة الجيولوجية المناخية تشمل مجموعة من التقنيات النظريّة، منها تقنيات إدارة الإشعاع الشمسي مثل نثر الهباء الجوي -جسيمات عاكسة صغيرة- في الستراتوسفير، لعكس جزء بسيط من ضوء الشمس إلى الفضاء، أو زيادة كمية الإشعاع الشمسي الذي يعود إلى الفضاء، ما يسهم في تبريد الكوكب، وهو أحد الحلول المطروحة لمعالجة مخاطر الاحتباس الحراري، ولا يوجد ما يؤكد استخدام هذه التقنية حتى اللحظة أو نثر الهباء الجوي لاختبارها.


وتنصح مجموعة كيث من يؤمن بهذه النظرية: 

“إذا كنت تؤمن بنظرية “الكيمتريل”، فاسأل نفسك كيف يمكنك أن تكون متأكداً إلى هذا الحد من وجود مؤامرة كبرى. فكّر في تفسيرات بديلة وبسيطة. تذكّر أن الإنترنت مليء بأشخاص متأكدين تماماً من أمور غير صحيحة. تذكّر أنه بينما تستطيع الحكومات إخفاء أسرار تخص عدداً قليلاً من الأشخاص، فإنها تُخفق في الحفاظ على سرية البرامج واسعة النطاق”.



أنجز تقرير تدقيق المعلومات المعمق بالتعاون بين أريج وأوزون.

المصدر: AFP

منار أبو حسون


تنتشر على مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي منشورات لما يعرف بـ”نظرية الكيمتريل”، وازدادت وتيرة هذا النوع من الادعاءات بعد الحرب الإقليمية في المنطقة، حيث روجت عدة حسابات لمزاعم تفيد بأن الجو أصبح أصفى نتيجة تراجع حركة الملاحة الجوية، ورش “غاز الكيميتريل” في الجو من قبل الطائرات التجارية لأهداف خفية؛ مثل التحكم بالمناخ أو التأثير في صحة البشر. 

تعود هذه الادعاءات إلى أواخر تسعينيات القرن الماضي، ضمن قائمة الادعاءات المتعلقة بـ”نظريات المؤامرة” التي تقوم على  فرضية وجود مخطط سري تديره جهات نافذة؛ للسيطرة على الأحداث والظواهر العالمية. وغالباً ما ترفض هذه النظريات الروايات الرسمية أو الإجماع العلمي، وتقدم تفسيرات بديلة تفتقر إلى الأدلة الموثوقة. 

يكشف هذا التقرير أبرز الادعاءات عن نظرية “غاز الكيمتريل”، التي تداولتها حسابات عربية على منصة “إكس” بعد الحرب الإقليمية الأخيرة منذ 28 شباط/فبراير 2026، حتى تاريخ نشر هذا التقرير، ويفند هذه الادعاءات استناداً إلى المصادر العلمية الموثوقة. 

ماذا يزعم مروجو “نظرية الكيمتريل”؟

تتبعنا عدداً من السرديات والمنشورات بمحتويات مختلفة، تروّج للنظرية عبر محتويات متنوعة، شملت مقاطع فيديو وصوراً ومنشورات نصية. ومن أبرزها ادعاء نشره حساب “خديجة أحمد” التي تعرف نفسها على أنها صيدلانية تروّج عبر حسابها لادعاءات متعلقة بنظريات المؤامرة، ومنها الكيمتريل.

أبرز هذه الادعاءات، التي نشرها هذا الحساب وحصد آلاف التفاعلات، كان بتاريخ 24 نيسان/أبريل 2026، زعم أن “غاز الكيمتريل” يُعد أحد أسباب التغير المناخي.


لقطة شاشة من حساب “خديجة خالد” للادعاء


وجاء في نص الادعاء: “هذا ما تفعله أمريكا وإسرائيل، يسرقون الأمطار، ينتجون سحب اصطناعية، يقومون بتلقيح السحب وتغيير المناخ، يرشون مادة “الكيمتريل”(Chemtrail)، يستخدمون تقنية “هارب” (Haarp). ولكن إذا سألتهم، سيقولون لك إن التغير في المناخ طبيعي“.

في اليوم نفسه، ردّ حساب “زهراء رمضان” على منشور “خديجة أحمد” مؤيداً تلك المزاعم، مدعياً أن “الخطوط البيضاء التي تتركها الطائرات في السماء، ليست مجرد بخار ماء، بل هي مواد كيميائية (مثل الباريوم والألمنيوم) ترشها “نخب سرية” لتقليل عدد السكان أو التلاعب بالمناخ“. 

ويُعد هذا الادعاء من أكثر الروايات تداولاً ضمن نظرية “الكيمتريل”؛ إذ تُرفق منشورات من هذا النوع عادةً بصور أو مقاطع فيديو لآثار التكاثف التي تخلّفها الطائرات في السماء، مع الادعاء بأنها تمثل “غاز الكيمتريل”، أما تسميته فجاءت من كلمتي “Chemical trials” أي المسارات الكيميائية.


لقطة شاشة من ادعاء “زهراء  رمضان” و “موزه بنت عبيد”


وفي سياق مماثل، نشر أحد الحسابات المروجة لنظريات المؤامرة من الكويت، والذي يعيد عادةً نشر هذا النوع من المحتوى من حسابات أجنبية، ادعاءً في 9 حزيران/يونيو 2026، زعم فيه أن وثائق لوكالة المخابرات المركزية الأمريكية (CIA) كشفت عن خطط أميركية للسيطرة على العالم، عبر التلاعب بالطقس باستخدام ما يُعرف بـ”الكيمتريل”.


صورة من ادعاء qqqq8118 لمشاركة منشور حساب يدعى Stern Drew 


كما تناولت  العديد من الحسابات مزاعم أن الجو أصبح أنقى عقب إغلاق المجال الجوي، بسبب الحرب الإقليمية وتوقف رش “الكيمتريل“. ومن أبرز هذه الحسابات، حساب “دكتور ياسر خالد العمار“، الذي يعرّف نفسه بأنه جراح عظام كويتي يتابعه نحو 77 ألف متابع، ويتبنى الحساب منذ سنوات نظرية رش الكيمتريل لحجب أشعة الشمس والتلاعب بالمناخ، ونشر خلال الحرب عدة منشورات ادعى فيها أن السماء أصبحت أصفى مع توقف رش غاز “الكميتريل“.


صورة لمنشورات على ” اكس” تدعي توقف رش الكيمتريل بسبب الحرب



أبرز الحسابات التي رصدناها والتي تروج لادعاءات الكيمتريل:

د. ياسر خالد العمار
76.9 ألف متابع
جراح عظام كويتي
خديجة أحمد
20.9 ألف متابع
صيدلانية
موزه بنت عبيد
20.3 ألف متابع
أخصائية تقويم أسنان من الإمارات
STOP Age.2030
21 ألف متابع
حساب يهدف لنشر الوعي بأضرار اللقاحات وكشف مافيا الطب والعلم المزور وأهداف أجندة 2030.

وبخصوص  الوثيقة التي يزعم أنها لـ(CIA)، بمراجعة هذه الوثائق من وكالة المخابرات المركزية التي رُفعت عنها السرية، لا يوجد فيها ما يثبت وجود خطة أميركية للسيطرة على العالم من خلال التحكم بالطقس، أو رش مبيدات أو مواد في الجو، ولا توجد أي إشارة لاسم “الكيمتريل”، وفحوى الوثيقة حول طموحات التحكم بالطقس في ذلك الوقت عام 1965.


هل هناك أي برامج علمية موثقة لإطلاق مواد في الجو؟

أكدت مجموعة كيث في جامعة هارفارد عدم وجود أي أدلة موثوقة تدعم نظرية مؤامرة “الكيمتريل”، موضحةً أنه ربما قد يخلط بعض الناس بين مفهوم الكيمتريل والهندسة الجيولوجية المناخية.

في مقابلة تفصيلية أجراها موقع “Carbon Brief” مع عالمة المناخ، الدكتورة كاثرين هايهو، أكدت فيها بأن “الهندسة الجيولوجية ليست هي الكيمتريل”، مؤكدة أن “الكيمتريل” ما هو إلا “نظرية مؤامرة”.

أما الهندسة الجيولوجية المناخية تشمل مجموعة من التقنيات النظريّة، منها تقنيات إدارة الإشعاع الشمسي مثل نثر الهباء الجوي -جسيمات عاكسة صغيرة- في الستراتوسفير، لعكس جزء بسيط من ضوء الشمس إلى الفضاء، أو زيادة كمية الإشعاع الشمسي الذي يعود إلى الفضاء، ما يسهم في تبريد الكوكب، وهو أحد الحلول المطروحة لمعالجة مخاطر الاحتباس الحراري، ولا يوجد ما يؤكد استخدام هذه التقنية حتى اللحظة أو نثر الهباء الجوي لاختبارها.


وتنصح مجموعة كيث من يؤمن بهذه النظرية: 

“إذا كنت تؤمن بنظرية “الكيمتريل”، فاسأل نفسك كيف يمكنك أن تكون متأكداً إلى هذا الحد من وجود مؤامرة كبرى. فكّر في تفسيرات بديلة وبسيطة. تذكّر أن الإنترنت مليء بأشخاص متأكدين تماماً من أمور غير صحيحة. تذكّر أنه بينما تستطيع الحكومات إخفاء أسرار تخص عدداً قليلاً من الأشخاص، فإنها تُخفق في الحفاظ على سرية البرامج واسعة النطاق”.



أنجز تقرير تدقيق المعلومات المعمق بالتعاون بين أريج وأوزون.

item.title: الفيديو المتداول الذي يُظهر جيمي كيميل يعلّق على مباراة مصر والأرجنتين مولد بالذكاء الاصطناعي
item.description:
في أعقاب فوز المنتخب الأرجنتيني على نظيره المصري في دور الـ16 من كأس العالم 2026، وما أثارته نتيجة المباراة من اعتراضات واسعة بين متابعي البطولة، بما في ذلك المنتخب المصري، تداولت حسابات على مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي، بتاريخ 8 تموز/يوليو 2026، مقطع فيديو زُعم أنه يُظهر المذيع الأميركي جيمي كيميل وهو يصف المباراة، التي انتهت بفوز الأرجنتين بثلاثة أهداف، بأنها “سرقة بنكية”.

وحظي المقطع بانتشار واسع، محققاً آلاف المشاهدات والتفاعلات (مثل هنا، وهنا)

وبالتحقق، تبيّن أن أقدم نسخة أمكن الوصول إليها للمقطع نُشرت بتاريخ 8 تموز/يوليو 2026 عبر حساب على تيك توك يحمل اسم “celebrity.park“، وقد صنّف ناشر الفيديو المحتوى بنفسه على أنه مولد بالذكاء الاصطناعي.



كما أظهر فحص محتوى الحساب أنه ينشر بصورة متكررة مقاطع فيديو مولدة بالذكاء الاصطناعي. كذلك، أظهرت نتائج أداة Hive Moderation أن احتمال كون الفيديو مولداً بالذكاء الاصطناعي يبلغ نحو 99%.



ولم نعثر أيضاً على أي أثر للمقطع أو للتصريح المنسوب إلى كيميل عبر الحسابات الرسمية لبرنامج Jimmy Kimmel Live، بما في ذلك حسابه على إنستغرام. إضافة إلى ذلك، كان كيميل في إجازته الصيفية ابتداءً من 7 تموز/يوليو، فيما تولّت مذيعة أخرى تقديم البرنامج خلال تلك الفترة.

item.title: الصورة المتداولة التي تُظهر دلال عريقات برفقة نتنياهو مولدة بالذكاء الاصطناعي
item.description:
في أعقاب منشور نشرته دلال عريقات، ابنة السياسي الفلسطيني صائب عريقات، في 11 تموز/يوليو 2026، تحدثت فيه عن مقابلة أجرتها مع مجلة “صبرا“، أكدت خلالها أن “مخاطبة الجمهور الإسرائيلي علناً ليست تطبيعاً ولا تنازلاً عن الرواية الفلسطينية”، تداولت حسابات على مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي صورة زُعم أنها تجمعها برئيس الوزراء الإسرائيلي بنيامين نتنياهو.

وبالتحقق، تبيّن أن أقدم نشر للصورة كان في اليوم نفسه عبر صفحة ساخرة على فيسبوك وتيلغرام تحمل اسم “مش هيك”، ونُشرت في سياق التعليق على تصريحات عريقات الأخيرة. كما لم نعثر على أي نسخة أقدم للصورة، أو على أي تقارير في وسائل إعلام فلسطينية أو إسرائيلية أو دولية موثوقة تشير إلى عقد لقاء بين دلال عريقات ونتنياهو.



ويظهر في الصورة شعار Gemini نموذج الذكاء الاصطناعي التابع لشركة غوغل، كما أظهرت نتائج أداة AI or Not المتخصصة في كشف الصور المولدة بالذكاء الاصطناعي أن الصورة يُرجح أنها مولدة بالذكاء الاصطناعي بنسبة تقارب 85%.



أما الصورة الثانية المتداولة، فأظهر البحث العكسي أن أقدم نسخة منها تعود إلى عام 2013، وتوثق استئناف المفاوضات الإسرائيلية – الفلسطينية في واشنطن بعد انقطاع دام 3 سنوات حينها، حيث جمعت كبير المفاوضين الفلسطينيين آنذاك صائب عريقات بوزيرة العدل الإسرائيلية السابقة تسيبي ليفني.

وخلال المقابلة التي أجرتها دلال عريقات في 10 تموز/يوليو 2026 مع الصحفي والباحث الفلسطيني ياسر مناع لصالح مجلة “صبرا“، الصادرة باللغة العبرية والموجهة إلى الجمهور الإسرائيلي، شددت على أن إيصال الرواية الفلسطينية إلى مختلف الجماهير يمثل جزءاً من المعركة السياسية والأخلاقية، حتى لا تترك الساحة لروايات أخرى لا تمثل الفلسطينيين.

item.title: Thirty-One Years After the Srebrenica Genocide: Preserving Facts, Honoring Victims and Supporting Survivors
item.description:
The Hague, 11 July 2026 – As families gather today at the Srebrenica Memorial Cemetery in Potočari to bury the newly identified remains of ten victims of the 1995 Srebrenica Genocide, the International Commission on Missing Persons (ICMP) joins them in honoring all those who were murdered.

This year’s commemoration follows the establishment by the United Nations of the International Day of Reflection and Commemoration of the 1995 Genocide in Srebrenica. In creating this International Day, the United Nations has reaffirmed the importance of preserving the facts established through judicial proceedings, honoring the victims, supporting survivors, combating genocide denial, preventing the glorification of convicted war criminals, and promoting education to help prevent future atrocities.

Over the past three decades, the effort to account for the missing has become one of the clearest demonstrations of these principles in practice. More than 90 percent of the more than 8,000 victims of the Srebrenica Genocide have been accounted for through scientific investigation and DNA-based identification. This unprecedented achievement has enabled families to recover and bury their loved ones while establishing an authoritative factual record that has supported criminal accountability and upheld the historical truth of the Genocide.

“The investigations into the Srebrenica Genocide demonstrated that even the most systematic attempts to conceal mass crimes can be overcome through science, independent institutions, international cooperation, and the rule of law,” said ICMP Director-General Kathryne Bomberger. “The painstaking work of recovering, identifying, and documenting thousands of victims helped establish the facts of the Genocide through judicial processes. That factual record remains one of the strongest safeguards against denial and historical revisionism. While approximately 1,000 people remain missing, States continue to have an obligation under international law to undertake effective investigations to account for them.”

The progress that has been achieved has been driven by the determination of families from communities across Bosnia and Herzegovina, whose insistence that every victim be found, identified, and returned transformed the international response to the issue of missing persons. The perseverance of families demonstrated that accounting for the missing is not only a humanitarian imperative, but also an essential component of justice and the rule of law.

Accounting for the missing from Srebrenica has been one of the most comprehensive scientific and investigative efforts ever undertaken following a mass atrocity. From the systematic recovery of human remains to the pioneering large-scale application of DNA identification, investigators connected victims from the locations where their remains were recovered to locations where they were executed, documenting the deliberate removal and reburial of bodies in secondary and tertiary graves in an effort to conceal the crime. By linking each identified victim to the circumstances of death and location of recovery, the process generated forensic and genetic evidence that supported investigations and was presented in 35 criminal trials before domestic courts and the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia. Together with judicial findings, this evidence established one of the most complete factual records ever made in relation to a mass atrocity.

Working with domestic authorities, families of the missing, civil society and the international community, ICMP helped to develop and implement this integrated, DNA based scientific approach and has helped to identify approximately 7,000 victims of the Srebrenica Genocide. The methodologies pioneered in Bosnia and Herzegovina have since been applied worldwide in support of governments addressing large numbers of missing persons from conflict, human rights abuses, disasters, organized crime, migration, and other causes.

Today, ICMP continues to help the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina to locate and identify those who are still missing, ensuring that scientific evidence supports judicial processes.

Launched on the 30th anniversary of the Srebrenica massacre, ICMP’s Geography of Genocide shows how decades of forensic archaeological, anthropological, genetic, and investigative work exposed the systematic effort to conceal the crime. The interactive platform illustrates the movement of victims’ remains from primary to secondary and tertiary graves and enables families to find out where the remains of their loved ones were recovered while helping the broader public to understand how scientific evidence established the historical record.

Thirty-one years after the Srebrenica Genocide, the work is not yet complete. Sustaining the effort to account for those who are still missing is an essential part of meeting States’ legal obligations, preserving the integrity of the historical record, and reinforcing the principles of truth and accountability.

About ICMP

ICMP is a treaty-based intergovernmental organization with Headquarters in The Hague, the Netherlands. Its mandate is to secure the cooperation of governments and others in locating missing persons resulting from conflict, human rights abuses, disasters, organized crime, migration, and other causes, and to assist them in doing so.

item.title: Trideset jedna godina nakon genocida u Srebrenici: čuvanje činjenica, odavanje počasti žrtvama i pružanje podrške preživjelima
item.description:
Hag, 11. juli 2026. godine – Dok se porodice danas okupljaju u Memorijalnom centru Srebrenica – Potočari kako bi ukopale novo-identificirane posmrtne ostatke deset žrtava genocida u Srebrenici iz 1995. godine, Međunarodna komisija za nestale osobe (ICMP) pridružuje im se u odavanju počasti svim ubijenim žrtvama.

Ovogodišnja komemoracija održava se nakon što su Ujedinjene nacije uspostavile Međunarodni dan sjećanja i obilježavanja genocida u Srebrenici iz 1995. godine. Uspostavljanjem ovog međunarodnog dana, Ujedinjene nacije su ponovno potvrdile važnost čuvanja činjenica utvrđenih u sudskim postupcima, odavanja počasti žrtvama, pružanja podrške preživjelima, suprotstavljanja negiranju genocida, sprečavanja veličanja osuđenih ratnih zločinaca te promicanja obrazovanja kako bi se spriječilo ponavljanje budućih zločina.

Tokom protekle tri decenije, nastojanja da se pronađu i identificiraju nestale osobe postala su jedan od najjasnijih primjera primjene ovih principa u praksi. Više od 90 procenata od preko 8.000 žrtava genocida u Srebrenici pronađeno je i identificirano zahvaljujući naučnim istragama i identifikaciji zasnovanoj na analizi DNK. Ovo dostignuće, bez premca u svijetu, omogućilo je porodicama da dostojanstveno pronađu i ukopaju svoje najmilije, istovremeno uspostavljajući vjerodostojan činjenični zapis koji je doprinio uspostavljanju krivične odgovornosti počinilaca i očuvanju historijske istine o genocidu.

“Istrage o genocidu u Srebrenici pokazale su da se čak i najsistematičniji pokušaji prikrivanja masovnih zločina mogu prevazići zahvaljujući nauci, nezavisnim institucijama, međunarodnoj saradnji i vladavini prava“, izjavila je generalna direktorica ICMP-a, Kathryne Bomberger. „Mukotrpan rad na pronalaženju, identifikaciji i dokumentovanju hiljada žrtava pomogao je da se kroz sudske postupke utvrde činjenice o genocidu. Taj činjenični zapis i dalje predstavlja jednu od najsnažnijih zaštita od negiranja i historijskog revizionizma. Iako se približno 1.000 osoba još uvijek vodi kao nestalo, države i dalje imaju obavezu prema međunarodnom pravu da provode djelotvorne istrage kako bi se utvrdila njihova sudbina.”

Napredak koji je ostvaren rezultat je odlučnosti porodica iz zajednica širom Bosne i Hercegovine, čije je insistiranje da svaka žrtva bude pronađena, identificirana i vraćena svojoj porodici promijenilo međunarodni pristup pitanju nestalih osoba. Ustrajnost porodica pokazala je da rasvjetljavanje sudbine nestalih nije samo humanitarni imperativ, već i suštinska komponenata pravde i vladavine prava.

Rasvjetljavanje sudbine nestalih iz Srebrenice predstavlja jedan od najsveobuhvatnijih naučnih i istražnih poduhvata ikada provedenih nakon nekog masovnog zločina. Od sistematske ekshumacije posmrtnih ostataka do pionirske primjene identifikacije na osnovu DNK u velikom obimu, istražitelji su povezali žrtve s mjestima na kojima su njihovi posmrtni ostaci pronađeni i mjestima na kojima su pogubljene, dokumentirajući namjerno premještanje i ponovno ukopavanje tijela u sekundarne i tercijarne masovne grobnice s ciljem prikrivanja zločina. Povezivanjem svake identificirane žrtve s okolnostima smrti i mjestom ekshumacije posmrtnih ostataka, prikupljeni su forenzički i genetski dokazi koji su potkrijepili istrage i korišteni kao dokazni materijal u 35 krivičnih postupaka pred domaćim sudovima i Međunarodnim krivičnim sudom za bivšu Jugoslaviju. Zajedno sa sudskim utvrđenim činjenicama, ovi dokazi čine jedan od najpotpunijih činjeničnih zapisa ikada uspostavljenih u vezi s nekim zločinom masovnih razmjera.

Sarađujući s domaćim vlastima, porodicama nestalih, organizacijama civilnog društva i međunarodnom zajednicom, ICMP je pomogao u razvoju i primjeni ovog integriranog naučnog pristupa zasnovanog na analizi DNK te je doprinio identifikaciji približno 7.000 žrtava genocida u Srebrenici. Metodologije po prvu put razvijene u Bosni i Hercegovini od tada se primjenjuju širom svijeta kao podrška vladama koje se suočavaju s velikim brojem nestalih osoba uslijed sukoba, povreda ljudskih prava, prirodnih katastrofa, organiziranog kriminala, migracija i drugih uzroka.

Danas ICMP nastavlja pružati podršku nadležnim organima Bosne i Hercegovine u pronalaženju i identifikaciji osoba koje se još uvijek vode kao nestale, osiguravajući da naučni dokazi i dalje budu temelj i podrška sudskim postupcima.

Pokrenuta povodom 30. godišnjice masakra u Srebrenici, ICMP-ova Geografija genocida prikazuje kako su decenije forenzičko-arheološkog, antropološkog, genetskog i istražnog rada razotkrile sistematske pokušaje prikrivanja zločina. Interaktivna platforma prikazuje premještanje posmrtnih ostataka žrtava iz primarnih u sekundarne i tercijarne masovne grobnice te omogućava porodicama da saznaju gdje su pronađeni posmrtni ostaci njihovih najmilijih, istovremeno pomažući široj javnosti da razumije kako su historijske činjenice utvrđene na osnovu naučnih dokaza.

Trideset jednu godinu nakon genocida u Srebrenici, ovaj posao još nije završen. Nastavak napora na pronalaženju i identifikaciji osoba koje se još uvijek vode kao nestale predstavlja ključni dio ispunjavanja zakonskih obaveza država, očuvanja integriteta historijskih činjenica i jačanja principa istine i odgovornosti.

O ICMP-u

ICMP je sporazumom utemeljena međunarodna organizacija sa sjedištem u Hagu u Nizozemskoj. Njegov mandat je da osigura saradnju vlada i drugih organa vlasti u pronalaženju osoba nestalih uslijed sukoba, povreda ljudskih prava, nesreća, organiziranog kriminala, migracija i drugih razloga, te da im pruži pomoć u tim procesima.

item.title: Thirty-One Years After the Srebrenica Genocide: Preserving Facts, Honoring Victims and Supporting Survivors
item.description:
The Hague, 11 July 2026 – As families gather today at the Srebrenica Memorial Cemetery in Potočari to bury the newly identified remains of ten victims of the 1995 Srebrenica Genocide, the International Commission on Missing Persons (ICMP) joins them in honoring all those who were murdered.

This year’s commemoration follows the establishment by the United Nations of the International Day of Reflection and Commemoration of the 1995 Genocide in Srebrenica. In creating this International Day, the United Nations has reaffirmed the importance of preserving the facts established through judicial proceedings, honoring the victims, supporting survivors, combating genocide denial, preventing the glorification of convicted war criminals, and promoting education to help prevent future atrocities.

Over the past three decades, the effort to account for the missing has become one of the clearest demonstrations of these principles in practice. More than 90 percent of the more than 8,000 victims of the Srebrenica Genocide have been accounted for through scientific investigation and DNA-based identification. This unprecedented achievement has enabled families to recover and bury their loved ones while establishing an authoritative factual record that has supported criminal accountability and upheld the historical truth of the Genocide.

“The investigations into the Srebrenica Genocide demonstrated that even the most systematic attempts to conceal mass crimes can be overcome through science, independent institutions, international cooperation, and the rule of law,” said ICMP Director-General Kathryne Bomberger. “The painstaking work of recovering, identifying, and documenting thousands of victims helped establish the facts of the Genocide through judicial processes. That factual record remains one of the strongest safeguards against denial and historical revisionism. While approximately 1,000 people remain missing, States continue to have an obligation under international law to undertake effective investigations to account for them.”

The progress that has been achieved has been driven by the determination of families from communities across Bosnia and Herzegovina, whose insistence that every victim be found, identified, and returned transformed the international response to the issue of missing persons. The perseverance of families demonstrated that accounting for the missing is not only a humanitarian imperative, but also an essential component of justice and the rule of law.

Accounting for the missing from Srebrenica has been one of the most comprehensive scientific and investigative efforts ever undertaken following a mass atrocity. From the systematic recovery of human remains to the pioneering large-scale application of DNA identification, investigators connected victims from the locations where their remains were recovered to locations where they were executed, documenting the deliberate removal and reburial of bodies in secondary and tertiary graves in an effort to conceal the crime. By linking each identified victim to the circumstances of death and location of recovery, the process generated forensic and genetic evidence that supported investigations and was presented in 35 criminal trials before domestic courts and the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia. Together with judicial findings, this evidence established one of the most complete factual records ever made in relation to a mass atrocity.

Working with domestic authorities, families of the missing, civil society and the international community, ICMP helped to develop and implement this integrated, DNA based scientific approach and has helped to identify approximately 7,000 victims of the Srebrenica Genocide. The methodologies pioneered in Bosnia and Herzegovina have since been applied worldwide in support of governments addressing large numbers of missing persons from conflict, human rights abuses, disasters, organized crime, migration, and other causes.

Today, ICMP continues to help the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina to locate and identify those who are still missing, ensuring that scientific evidence supports judicial processes.

Launched on the 30th anniversary of the Srebrenica massacre, ICMP’s Geography of Genocide shows how decades of forensic archaeological, anthropological, genetic, and investigative work exposed the systematic effort to conceal the crime. The interactive platform illustrates the movement of victims’ remains from primary to secondary and tertiary graves and enables families to find out where the remains of their loved ones were recovered while helping the broader public to understand how scientific evidence established the historical record.

Thirty-one years after the Srebrenica Genocide, the work is not yet complete. Sustaining the effort to account for those who are still missing is an essential part of meeting States’ legal obligations, preserving the integrity of the historical record, and reinforcing the principles of truth and accountability.

About ICMP

ICMP is a treaty-based intergovernmental organization with Headquarters in The Hague, the Netherlands. Its mandate is to secure the cooperation of governments and others in locating missing persons resulting from conflict, human rights abuses, disasters, organized crime, migration, and other causes, and to assist them in doing so.

item.title: Same government, more victims: Access Now calls for an urgent investigation into hacking of MEP
item.description:
Home / Press Releases / Same government, more victims: Access Now calls for an urgent investigation into hacking of MEP

Access Now joins more than 30 human rights organizations and individuals in condemning the Pegasus spyware attack against Stelios Kouloglou, a Greek journalist and then-Member of the European Parliament, while he was serving on the PEGA Committee, a European Parliament committee that investigated Pegasus and other spyware abuses, as revealed by the Citizen Lab. Citizen Lab’s report indicates that Kouloglou’s iPhone was infected with Pegasus spyware on or around October 21, 2022, and again on March 6 and 7, 2023.

Access Now is especially concerned about Citizen Lab’s shocking finding that on or around October 21, 2022, Kouloglou’s iPhone was hacked by the same government that also targeted several victims in our joint 2024 investigation of Pegasus hacking of Russian- and Belarusian-speaking journalists and activists based in the EU. According to the Citizen Lab’s forensic analysis, on that day, Kouloglou was targeted from the same Apple ID  — rauharepo888[@]gmail.com —  as several of the victims named in the report. Citizen Lab has no evidence that the hacking was the work of the Greek, Russian, or Belarusian government.

Citizen Lab’s report indicates that Kouloglou was hacked during key periods of PEGA Committee activity and would have likely allowed the attacker to capture non-public information about committee activities, including preparations for the publication of its first draft report. On the date of the first documented infection, Kouloglou was in the hospital and was visited by Greek investigative journalist Thanasis Koukakis, who had testified to the PEGA Committee the previous month as he was himself targeted with Intellexa’s Predator spyware. The timing suggests that the attacker was likely interested in monitoring Kouloglou’s activities and communications related to the PEGA Committee.

Access Now and civil society partners recommend the EU conduct an independent and impartial investigation into the hacking of Kouloglou, determine the full scope of the spyware targeting of the PEGA Committee, provide effective remedies to the affected victims, and implement the PEGA Committee’s recommendations.

Read the full statement.
